newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 22.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- HOLD INTEREST RATES, CBI SAYS

The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) has backed chancellor Kenneth Clarke's policy of keeping interest rates static after releasing details of its latest quarterly survey which shows booked export orders falling for the first time in more than three years. Clarke resisted calls last week from the governor of the Bank of England to increase interest rates, pointing to the strength of the pound. The CBI also pointed to the strength of sterling as the reason for the fall in export orders.
-- BOEING DROPS PLAN TO BUILD 550-SEAT AIRCRAFT

US aircraft manufacturer Boeing has dropped plans for a 550-seat "super-jumbo" plane, leaving the way clear for the rival European group Airbus Industrie to proceed with its own large jet. Boeing claimed that the market for an aircraft larger than its 400-seater 747 would not justify the $7 billion cost of developing the super-jumbo. Airbus says it is still talking to 19 airlines about its proposed 550-seat aircraft, the A3XX.
-- HESELTINE WAR OF WORDS OVER BUSINESS REPORT

Michael Heseltine, deputy leader of the Conservative party, has become involved in a war of words with some of Britain's most senior businessmen after accusing them of being tools of the Labour party. Heseltine attacked businessmen involved in the Commission on Public Policy and British Business, a group which has backed some of the key policies of the Labour party, including support for the European social chapter for a proposed national minimum wage. In a letter to the Financial Times, the Commission responded by expressing "surprise" at the outburst and denied that it had any party political agenda.
-- DRESDNER LOOKS TO BUY UK FUND MANAGEMENT GROUP

German commercial bank Dresdner Bank has said it is looking at buying another UK fund management group to add to Kleinwort Benson, the UK investment bank it already owns. The announcement, made by Dresdner director Gerhard Eberstadt, will reassure leaders of the UK's fund management industry after fears that the publicity of the Nicola Horlick case would damage its reputation. Eberstadt said that "Britain is one of the most interesting markets in asset management".
-- NEW NISSAN MODEL TO CREATE 800 UK JOBS

Japanese car maker Nissan has announced plans to build a third model at its factory at Sunderland, NE England. The move, planned for 2000, will create 800 jobs. The new model, which will require a 215 million sterling investment by Nissan and its suppliers, will be a lower-mid-sized car to fit between the Micra hatchback and Primera sedan. It is also expected to create a further 2,700 jobs in the UK components industry.
-- ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND OFFERS INTERNET SERVICES

The Royal Bank of Scotland is offering the UK's first full banking service on the Internet, including a guarantee to refund any transaction which the customer has not authorised. The service will use encryption technology to scramble data and authorise passwords, and it will also only work on PCs which have been specifically registered by the customer.
-- UNIONS SNUB FORD ON "CLASSIC" ESCORT FOR HALEWOOD

Unions representing workers at Ford's Halewood plant on Merseyside, which is due to lose 1,300 jobs, have dismissed as a "sham" proposals by Ford to allow the plant to build the current Escort as a "classic" model when production of a newer Escort model is switched elsewhere. The unions dispute claims by Ford that there will be sufficient demand for the Classic model when the new model is also on sale. Ford workers are preparing to call a ballot for industrial action over the job losses at Halewood.
-- LANG BLOCKS BID FOR MID KENT

In a move which could herald an end to consolidation in the water industry, Trade Secretary Ian Lang has blocked a hostile takeover bid for water supply company Mid Kent. The move follows a partial blocking by Lang three months ago of a potential auction for another water company, Southwest Water. On that occasion Lang cited the adverse impact on competition in an essentially monopolistic industry. The bidders for Mid Kent, Generale des Eaux and Saur, already own two water companies sharing boundaries with Mid Kent.
-- ALLIED IRISH BUYS AMERICAN BANK FOR 810 MILLION STG

Allied Irish Bank has acquired Dauphin Deposit Corp, a Pennsylvania bank holding company, for $1.36 billion (810 million stg). The move will strengthen AIB's US retail banking operation, boosting the size of its US subsidiary First Maryland Bancorp by over 50 percent and taking its total assets to $16.8 billion. It will also expand its territory from its Baltimore-Washington base into neighboring Pennsylvania.
-- LIFE SCIENCES BACKS THERMO BID

Life Sciences International, the UK-based laboratory equipment maker, saw its shares rise 41.5p to 134p on Tuesday after it recommended a 235.9 million stg bid from Thermo Instrument Systems, the world's largest manufacturer of scientific analytical instruments. Thermo, which acquired the scientific instruments business of Fisons for 202 million stg in 1995, will add research and clinical equipment to its portfolio if the Life Sciences deal is approved.
